applicant_utility.summary: Australia Awards pays the full package - tuition, return airfare, a contribution to living expenses and medical insurance - but it is a development award, so the final step is binding: you must go home for a minimum of two years after your degree to contribute to development in your field. Applications run only in the annual 1 February - 30 April window through OASIS, and the Bangladesh page now says applications are closed and reopen in early 2027. Because no stipend figure is published, do your own cost survey of the Australian city you intend to study in before committing.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early and mid-career professionals from target sectors who intend to return and apply their degree to development work at home.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your course and university are on the participating list before the February window opens
Prepare the OASIS online application and the country-specific eligibility documents before 30 April
Be ready to accept the two-year home-country return requirement in the scholarship contract
Check medical insurance is active for arrival, since insurance is part of the published award benefits
common_rejection_risks: Applying outside the narrow 1 February - 30 April window
Choosing a course or institution that is not a participating one for your country
Overlooking the two-year home-country return condition, which is enforced through the contract
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Personal costs beyond the published benefits; the programme's stipend rate is not published on the pages checked, so budget independently for the receiving city.
document_audit: Eligibility criteria are country-specific and published per country before applications open - check your country's page, not the general regional text
alerts: Applications for the 2026 round are closed as of 10 October 2026; the next round reopens in early 2027
The programme is managed in South Asia and Mongolia by Palladium on behalf of the Australian Government
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Watch your country's Australia Awards page from January, apply in OASIS inside the window, then follow the country selection process through interview and offer.

applicant_utility.summary: This row is a duplicate label problem rather than a live scholarship: the Netherlands Fellowship Programme (and the Orange Knowledge Programme that succeeded it) no longer run - the official Study in NL hub confirms OKP ended in 2024 and lists only MSP, Erasmus+ and the NL Scholarship as Nuffic-administered awards. If your degree is not sponsored under one of those, OTS-style support is arranged directly with individual Dutch universities, without any central Nuffic page, deadline or amount. Treat any site advertising 'NFP/OTS 2027' with suspicion and go to the university's own funding page instead.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students assessing current Dutch options rather than this legacy label - realistically the NL Scholarship (Holland Scholarship), Erasmus+ or a university bursary.

Check the MENA Scholarship Programme eligibility only if you are from an eligible MENA country
common_rejection_risks: Preparing an application for a programme that no longer exists

document_audit: Any OTS-style bursary is administered by the university itself, so documentation follows that university's own rules
